The '''2018–19 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Iowa]] during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by ninth-year head coach [[Fran McCaffery]] and played their home games at [[Carver–Hawkeye Arena]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Hawkeyes finished the season 23–12, 10–10 in [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in sixth place. They defeated [[2018–19 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] in the second round of the [[2019 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] before losing to [[2018–19 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 10 seed in the South region. There they defeated No. 7-seeded [[2018–19 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] in the First Round before losing to No. 2-seeded [[2018–19 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] in the Second Round.

==Previous season==
The [[2017–18 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Hawkeyes]] finished the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] 14–19, 4–14 in [[2017–18 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a three-way tie for 11th place. As the No. 12 seed in the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2017–18 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] before losing to [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the second round.

==Schedule and results==
The 2018–19 season will mark the first time in [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] history that the teams will play a 20-game conference schedule, setting a precedent for all Division I basketball.<ref name=":02">{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/big-ten-adds-two-games-for-a-20-game-conference-schedule-starting-in-2018-19/|title=Big Ten adds two games for a 20-game conference schedule starting in 2018–19 |last=Norlander|first=Matt|date=October 19, 2017|work=CBS Sports|access-date=March 9, 2018}}</ref> The new schedule will also include a regional component to increase the frequency of games among teams in similar areas. Over the course of a six-year cycle (12 playing opportunities), in-state rivals will play each other 12 times, regional opponents will play 10 times, and all other teams will play nine times.<ref name=":02" /> Three in-state series will be guaranteed home-and-homes: Illinois and Northwestern, Indiana and Purdue, and Michigan and Michigan State will always play twice.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21076233/big-ten-play-20-game-conference-schedule-next-season|title=Big Ten to move to 20-game conference slate |work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-03-12}}</ref>
